incidente.resumo: On July 18th, 2018, Allegro was unavailable for about twenty minutes after a special offer attracted more traffic than anticipated; a misconfiguration made some services reserve far more cluster resources than they needed, preventing new instances from starting although CPU and RAM were available. Service became responsive again around 12:20 after continued scaling, adding resources to the cluster and shutting down non-critical services.

descricao.texto: At 11:55 a further traffic increase caused response times of major services to rise.
trechos: At 11:55, further traffic increase caused response times of major services to rise, forcing us to scale out these services.

gatilho.texto: A special offer selling one hundred phones for PLN 1 attracted more traffic than anticipated; just before noon traffic peaked at 200%-300% of the previous day's traffic.
trechos:
The direct cause
was a special offer in which one hundred Honor 7C phones whose regular price is around PLN 850 (about € 200),
were offered at a price of PLN 1 (less than € 1).
Also just before noon, traffic peaked at 200%-300% of the traffic from previous day, depending on service.

descricao.texto: Due to a misconfiguration, some services reserved much more cluster resources than they needed; reserved resources cannot be used by other instances, so new service instances could not be started even though plenty of CPU and RAM was available.
trechos: As we later found out, due to a misconfiguration, some services reserved much more resources than they actually needed.
These resources are reserved for a particular instance and can’t be used by others even if the owner is not really consuming them.
This prevented more instances from starting despite resources being there.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The autoscaler did not respond quickly enough to rising traffic, and there were bad interactions between the autoscaler scaling services up and the cluster watchdog killing unresponsive instances.
trechos: During the outage, autoscaler did not respond quickly enough to rising traffic and we had to scale up manually.
There were also some bad interactions between the autoscaler scaling services up and the cluster watchdog killing off unresponsive instances.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Increased response times caused some Opbox instances to not report health status correctly, and from 12:05 the cluster killed unresponsive instances; new Opbox instances quickly became unresponsive under high load and were killed.
trechos: Increased response times caused some Opbox instances to not report their health status to the cluster correctly and at 12:05 the cluster started killing off unresponsive instances.
Newly started instances very quickly reached “unresponsive” status and were automatically killed.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Some backend services ran out of connection pools and associated file descriptors and became unresponsive even though CPU and RAM were available.
trechos: If we run out of them, our service becomes unresponsive even if CPU and RAM are available, and this is what happened to some of the backend services during the outage.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The text notes that when the whole cluster is maxed out, retries only increase the load; a circuit breaker should then stop further requests, but one circuit breaker between services was misconfigured with a failure threshold so high it was not reached during the surge.
trechos: However, if the whole cluster is maxed out, retries only increase the load while the whole request fails anyway.

In such a situation, a circuit breaker should prevent further requests, but as we found out during postmortem analysis, one of the circuit breakers between our services was not correctly configured: the failure threshold for triggering it was set to a high value which we didn’t reach even during such a serious surge in traffic.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Rate limiter coverage of the site was incomplete, and the rate limiters' "blank page" had an internal retry that kept generating requests; users manually refreshing and searching added further load.
trechos: Unfortunately, the coverage of the site by rate limiters was not complete, so while some pages were protected very well, others were not.
The “blank page” had an internal retry, so a user looking at such a page was actually still generating requests to the system once in a while, further increasing the load.

On the other hand, upon seeing that the site was broken, some users tried to manually refresh the pages they were viewing or to enter allegro.pl into the address bar and searching for the phone’s name, thus generating even more search requests manually.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: A direct link to the offer's item page had been published before the offer started, and the traffic was in large part bots rather than human users.
trechos: The special offer was to start at noon sharp, and a direct link to its item page had been published before.
Interestingly enough, the traffic which brought us down, was in large part bots rather than human users.

passos.texto: The team scaled out major services manually and the autoscaler started new Search instances, but resource reservations limited how far they could scale.
trechos: It was still quite high, though, and autoscaler started to spin up new instances of Search service.
We manually added even more instances, but the resource reservations created previously prevented us from scaling up as far as to decrease response times significantly.

passos.texto: Before 12:15 the team started adding more resources to the cluster and shutting down some non-critical services to free CPU and memory; around 12:20 the situation was under control and Allegro became responsive again.
trechos: While automated and manual scaling efforts continued, before 12:15 we started adding more resources to the cluster.
At the same time, we started shutting down some non-critical services in order to free CPU and memory.
Around 12:20, the situation was fully under control and Allegro became responsive again.

acoes.texto: Planned: change the cluster's approach to reserving resources so that resources are not locked out of the pool if they are not really used.
trechos: As the probably most important action resulting from this postmortem, we plan to change the cluster’s approach to reserving resources so that there is less waste and resources are not locked out of the pool if they are not really used.

acoes.texto: Better tune the configuration of thread and connection pools and retry policies.
trechos: By better tuning the configuration of thread and connection pools as well as the retry policies, we will be able to mitigate the impact of high traffic the next time it happens.

acoes.texto: Fix the misconfigured circuit breaker threshold and add an additional layer of circuit breakers directly after the frontend service.
trechos: In such a situation, a circuit breaker should prevent further requests, but as we found out during postmortem analysis, one of the circuit breakers between our services was not correctly configured: the failure threshold for triggering it was set to a high value which we didn’t reach even during such a serious surge in traffic.
Apart from fixing this, we are also adding an additional layer of circuit breakers directly after the frontend service.

acoes.texto: Try out ideas to make Opbox start up faster even under a high request load.
trechos: We will try out several ideas which should make the service start up faster even if it gets hit with lots of requests right away.

acoes.texto: Planned: a mechanism to tell backend services to generate simplified, cacheable responses under special conditions to decrease load under heavy traffic.
trechos: However, we plan to introduce a mechanism which will be able to tell backend services to generate simplified, cacheable responses under special conditions.
This will allow us to decrease load under heavy traffic.

acoes.texto: Planned: make it harder for bots to participate in this kind of offer.
trechos: Since we want to create a level playing field for all users, we plan to make it harder for bots to participate in this kind of offers.
On July 18th, 2018, at noon, Allegro went down and was unavailable for twenty minutes.
